summaries.gardner: Seagate shows some Rule Breaker traits, such as strong share-price momentum (up about 191% over 52 weeks), a technology lead in HAMR and a secular AI data tailwind. But it is a 1979-founded leader of a mature, cyclical industry rather than a top dog in an emerging one, and it lacks a consumer-loved brand. It fits Gardner's approach only partially.
summaries.buffett: Buffett would value the three-player industry structure and the current cash generation ($3.1B free cash flow in FY2026). He would be wary of the heavy cyclicality (a $529M loss in FY2023, revenue barely above FY2016's $11.2B) and of a price near 46 times trailing earnings and 67 times book. It is not a classic Buffett business with predictable long-term earnings.
summaries.munger: Munger would recognise the rational oligopoly and the hard-won HAMR know-how. He would worry, thinking backwards, about technology substitution by flash, capacity additions (Toshiba plans to double output) and the commodity-like history of disk drives. A great business at a fair price is hard to argue when margins are at a cyclical peak.
summaries.lynch: In Lynch's terms Seagate is a cyclical. Earnings are surging (GAAP EPS $13.90 in FY2026 vs $6.77, consensus FY2027 EPS about $36) and the forward P/E of about 17.6 looks low. Lynch warned that low P/Es on cyclicals near peak earnings can be a trap, so timing the cycle is the key question.
summaries.fisher: Seagate fits Fisher's emphasis on R&D that produces results: about two decades of HAMR work is now shipping in volume, and Mozaic 5 is planned for qualification in late 2027. Its sales organisation is strong with hyperscalers through long-term agreements. But profit margins have historically been volatile and management is not distinctive on long-range people policies, so the fit is partial.
summaries.graham: Seagate fails most of Graham's defensive-investor tests. It lost money in FY2023, suspended its dividend in 2009 (reinstated in April 2011), and trades at roughly 46 times trailing earnings and 67 times book value. Only its size and ten-year EPS growth ($0.82 in FY2016 to $13.90 in FY2026) pass.
summaries.thiel: Seagate has a hard-to-copy technology in HAMR and sits in an industry with only three players, which echoes Thiel's view of durable monopoly-like positions. But its technology is incrementally rather than ten times better than rivals', it did not start as a monopoly of a small market, and flash memory is a long-term substitution threat.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner focuses on companies riding a big platform shift (AI) with improving fundamentals at a fair price. Seagate's revenue is set to grow about 55% in FY2027 on consensus, with a PEG of about 0.26, which fits well. The open questions are cycle risk and whether the 2026 peak in margins holds once Toshiba adds capacity.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller-style analysis would like the accelerating earnings, rising estimates and a strong AI demand narrative over the next 18-24 months. The roughly 20% fall in the month to mid-October 2026 after Toshiba's capacity news shows how quickly sentiment can turn. It fits as a momentum and earnings-revision idea rather than a long-term holding.
summaries.smith: Terry Smith seeks consistently high returns on capital, high gross margins and resilience; Seagate's 45.6% FY2026 gross margin and high current ROIC are recent and cyclical. A loss in FY2023 and a 37% revenue drop that year fail his consistency test, and the valuation is far from 'don't overpay'. It is not a typical Fundsmith holding.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula, Seagate's return on capital is currently very high (ROIC about 86% TTM), but its earnings yield is low (EV/EBIT about 35, so operating profit is only about 2.9% of enterprise value). It would not rank near the top of a Magic Formula screen today.
summaries.akre: Akre's three-legged stool needs an extraordinary business, talented and honest management, and the ability to reinvest at high rates. Seagate scores on management execution and recent returns, but a cyclical commodity-like product and limited reinvestment needs (capex 4-6% of revenue, most cash returned or used to cut debt) make it a weak fit.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai's Dhandho approach wants a simple business in a temporary setback, bought at a big discount with little downside. Seagate is simple to understand, but it is at a cyclical high, not a setback, and the price assumes continued strength, so the heads-I-win, tails-I-don't-lose-much setup is missing.
summaries.wood: ARK focuses on disruptive platforms whose costs fall rapidly. Seagate supplies storage for AI data but is a 47-year-old incumbent whose main long-run threat is flash, a disruptive technology. It is a beneficiary of AI rather than an ARK-style disruptive innovator.
summaries.ackman: Ackman looks for simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generating businesses with dominant positions and high barriers to entry. Seagate has the barriers (three-player industry) and strong current free cash flow, but its earnings are not predictable through the cycle and its balance sheet only recently returned to positive equity. It is only a partial fit.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep's 'scale economics shared' model, in which a company passes scale savings to customers, does not describe Seagate, which is currently raising price per exabyte about 10% a year while supply is tight. Its edge is technology and industry structure rather than a self-reinforcing customer flywheel.
summaries.valentine: Don Valentine backed companies that solve big problems in huge markets with exceptional teams. Seagate solves a large, real problem, storing the world's exploding data cheaply, but it is a mature public incumbent rather than an early-stage company attacking a new market.
summaries.nash: Seagate passes many of Nash's growth and profitability tests: revenue grew 34% in FY2026, the operating margin was 33.6%, it has beaten consensus every recent quarter and the PEG is about 0.26. It fails his instant-kill on debt ($3.57B debt vs $1.70B cash at July 2026), and his DCF does not support today's price at a 12% discount rate. Heavy insider selling while the stock ran also counts against it.

momentum.evidence: STX is up about 191% over 52 weeks and about 132% year to date to $639.01 (Oct 16, 2026), far ahead of the market, despite a roughly 20% drop in the past month.

g4.evidence: CEO Dave Mosley (PhD physicist, CEO since 2017) has executed well recently, and institutions own about 85% of shares, but no famous anchor investor or partner is publicly associated with the stock.

g6.evidence: Some commentators call the run 'frothy' and the stock trades at about 46x trailing earnings and 67x book, but the consensus has a Strong Buy rating with an average target of about $1,138.

simple.evidence: Seagate makes and sells hard drives, mostly to cloud data centers, a business a careful generalist can understand.

b2.evidence: Results swing with the cycle: revenue fell from $11.7B in FY2022 to $6.6B in FY2024 with a $529M loss in FY2023, then rose to a record $12.2B in FY2026.

integrity.evidence: Management has been candid on capacity discipline and cut debt by $1.4B in FY2026, but the CEO sold large amounts of stock under a 10b5-1 plan in 2026 and the company paid a $300M US export penalty in 2023 over Huawei sales.

b6.evidence: Mosley publicly refused to build new factories (May 2026), choosing to grow by adding terabytes per disk rather than adding capacity or acquiring rivals.

roic.evidence: ROIC is about 86% on a trailing basis and FY2026 net income was $3.18B, but returns were negative in FY2023 and equity was negative until FY2026 because of debt-funded payouts.

fcf.evidence: FY2026 free cash flow was $3,105M on net income of $3,184M (operating cash flow $3,674M less $569M capex).

b10.evidence: Seagate pays out most of its cash flow, yet its market value has risen to about $145B as earnings rose from $1.3B in FY2021 to $3.2B in FY2026, far more than the profit it kept.

safety.evidence: At $639 the stock trades at about 46x trailing earnings and a 2.1% free-cash-flow yield, so there is no margin of safety against a conservative value.

fairprice.evidence: The forward P/E of about 17.6 and PEG of about 0.26 look reasonable if FY2027 consensus EPS of about $36 is achieved, but those are peak-cycle earnings.

mu5.evidence: It could be hurt by an AI/cloud capex pause, Toshiba's planned capacity doubling, Western Digital's HAMR catch-up, flash substitution, or customer concentration (one customer was 14% of FY2026 revenue).

reinvest.evidence: It needs little capital (capex 4-6% of revenue) and reinvests mainly in HAMR R&D ($755M product development in FY2026); most cash goes to debt reduction, dividends and buybacks.

ly2.evidence: It is a classic cyclical: an AI-driven upcycle in nearline storage after the FY2023 slump.

ly3.evidence: The forward P/E of about 17.6 is below expected EPS growth (consensus FY2027 EPS about $36 vs $15.58 non-GAAP in FY2026), a PEG of about 0.26.

runway.evidence: Management targets mid-20% annual exabyte growth for several years, but revenue growth depends on pricing and the cycle, and FY2026 revenue was only about 9% above FY2016's $11.2B.

ly7.evidence: Insiders are selling (the CEO sold 11,002 shares on Oct 1, 2026 alone under a 10b5-1 plan) and the share count rose about 5.5% year on year.

ly8.evidence: It is widely covered (26 analysts) and has been a high-profile AI storage trade in 2026.

fi2.evidence: Seagate is moving from Mozaic 3+ (30TB+) to Mozaic 4+ (up to 44TB) and plans Mozaic 5 qualification shipments in late calendar 2027.

fi3.evidence: Its long HAMR program now ships in volume (about 40% of nearline exabytes exiting FY2026) and helped lift gross margin to 52.3% in the June 2026 quarter.

fi4.evidence: It sells effectively to hyperscalers through long-term agreements covering most nearline exabytes through 2028, but this reflects industry supply tightness more than unusual sales skill.

longterm.evidence: It funded about two decades of HAMR development through downturns and is choosing capacity discipline over short-term volume grabs.

gr1.evidence: Revenue was $12.2B in FY2026 and the market value is about $145B.

ni10.evidence: Seagate reported a net loss of $529M in FY2023.

gr4.evidence: Seagate suspended its dividend in 2009 and reinstated it only in April 2011.

eps10.evidence: GAAP diluted EPS rose from $0.82 in FY2016 to $13.90 in FY2026.

gr6.evidence: The trailing P/E is about 46, far above 15 times average earnings.

gr7.evidence: P/E of about 46 times P/B of about 67 is far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: HAMR gives a meaningful capacity-per-disk lead (up to 44TB), not a tenfold advantage over Western Digital's drives.

timing.evidence: AI data growth and tight HDD supply let Seagate raise prices with nearline exabytes up 43% year on year in the June 2026 quarter, just as HAMR reaches volume.

th3.evidence: Seagate has been a large player in a large hard drive market for decades rather than starting from a dominant share of a small niche.

team.evidence: Management is experienced and executing well (record FY2026 results), but it is not widely regarded as a world-class or founder-led team.

th5.evidence: It has direct, multi-year supply relationships with every major cloud provider, plus OEM and distributor channels worldwide.

durable.evidence: The three-player structure and HAMR know-how should hold for years, but flash memory falling in cost could shrink the hard drive market over 10-20 years.

th7.evidence: Its early, long-term HAMR bet was a contrarian choice that now gives it a lead, though rivals are pursuing similar technology.

trend.evidence: It is a leading supplier of mass storage for AI and cloud data, with data center sales at 81% of Q4 FY2026 revenue.

dr1.evidence: GAAP EPS doubled to $13.90 in FY2026, Q1 FY2027 guidance is $7.30 non-GAAP EPS, and brokers such as Rosenblatt raised FY2027-FY2028 estimates in July 2026.

dr2.evidence: Mozaic 4+ mix and long-term contract pricing should lift margins, but Toshiba's capacity doubling by fiscal 2027 could weigh on pricing within that window.

dr4.evidence: Strong AI data center spending helps, but the business is economically sensitive (beta about 2.1) and still carries $3.6B of debt.

dr6.evidence: Q1 FY2027 results around Oct 27, 2026 (guidance $4.1B revenue), the Mozaic 4+ ramp and debt reduction to about $2.4B are near-term catalysts.

dr7.evidence: Earnings momentum is strong, but cyclicality and the stock's 20% one-month drop argue against a very large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: Gross margin reached 45.6% in FY2026 and 52.3% in the June 2026 quarter, high for hardware but up from 18.3% in FY2023.

fcfyield.evidence: The trailing free-cash-flow yield is about 2.1%, thin for a cyclical hardware company even with fast growth.

gb2.evidence: EV/EBIT is about 35, so operating profit is only about 2.9% of enterprise value.

pa2.evidence: The industry is in an upcycle with record results, not a temporary setback.

pa4.evidence: The business is strongly cash-generative and has three-player economics, but at a peak-cycle valuation a downturn could cause large, lasting losses for buyers at today's price.

wo1.evidence: It is a leading supplier of storage for AI data but not an AI technology leader itself.

wo2.evidence: HAMR lowers cost per terabyte as capacity per disk rises, but Seagate is currently raising price per exabyte rather than passing savings on.

wo3.evidence: It is focused on one platform, magnetic data storage.

wo4.evidence: Management targets mid-20% exabyte growth, which is strong but not a market many times larger in five years.

ac3.evidence: Results depend heavily on the cloud capex cycle and the economy; revenue fell 37% in FY2023.

ns1.evidence: Seagate is raising price per exabyte (about 10% year on year in Q4 FY2026) rather than sharing scale savings with customers.

ns4.evidence: HAMR leadership may strengthen its position, but Toshiba's expansion and flash substitution make a clearly stronger position in 10-20 years uncertain.

va2.evidence: Storing the world's fast-growing data cheaply is a large, painful problem for cloud providers.

tn1.evidence: It sells into the AI data trend as an infrastructure supplier, but it is a 1979-founded drive maker benefiting from the trend rather than a company built for it.

tn10.evidence: No major pending case is known, but it faces US export-control risk and paid a $300M BIS penalty in 2023 over Huawei sales.

tn11.evidence: Seagate provides high-capacity hard drives that help cloud and AI data centers store vast amounts of data at the lowest cost per terabyte, and charges per drive under multi-year supply agreements.
